quote: My normal goal is to uncover face-down cards on the column with the most face-down cards. At the beginning of the game, I do this by selecting the right-most card that is playable.
summary: 3♠b uncovers column e (4 face-down), the most of any column a play could uncover; e is also the right-most column with a playable card.

quote: Now playing 2♥ will uncover a face-down card on the pile with the most face-down cards AND a playable card. The overarching strategy is to uncover the card on the columns that has the most potential to reveal more cards to be played.
summary: 2♥b uncovers column d (3 face-down), the most among columns with a playable card; the stated aim is the most potential to reveal more playable cards.

quote: The 8♣ has the most potential to reveal more cards in the tableau.
summary: 8♣a uncovers column c (2 face-down); the other card play, 9♥f, would empty column a and uncover nothing.

quote: An ace always goes straight to home since not playing it has the most downside (covering a face-down card, blocking a column from accepting a high card, preventing the next card in the home pile from being played, etc.). Moving an ace to home has only upside consequences.
summary: A♦h: an ace goes home whenever it can; here it also uncovered column c.

quote: Both red 9s are exposed and could be played on the X♣, but I don't want to make that decision prematurely. I know they're availabe to play, but not playing either of them until I have a king to put in the columns is an unnecessary decision that locks me into a position before I know what's coming next. Leaving them in place leaves my options open;  so I'll draw.
summary: Drew instead of 9♥f or 9♦f: both red 9s compete for X♣, and either would empty a column with no king to fill it; the choice is deferred until more is known.

quote: No new play, so I'll draw.
summary: The turned cards (4♣ J♣ X♦) made no new play; the plays still available are the same ones deferred at #5, so draw again.

quote: The 7♦w-a is the only new play, so I'll play it.
summary: 7♦a is the only play that wasn't already available (the others are the deferred 9s and 8♣c), so it is played.

quote: No new play, so I'll draw.
summary: Nothing new became playable, so draw.

quote: The 6♠ is the only new play. It also happens to be the one play with the most potential to reveal the most face-down tableau cards, which matches my usual play logic, so I view it as an unforced "bonus" that supports making the play.
summary: 6♠a: new_play is the deciding reason; most_hidden (column g, 6 face-down) agrees and is called an unforced bonus.
The revealed 6♦ made no new play; draw.
J♠ on the waste made no new play; draw.
4♥ on the waste made no new play; draw.

quote: With the king available on the waste pile, I decide which red 9 to play on X♣. When there is nothing else to consider, as is the case here, I play the 9 with the most run-cards on it. There may be no advantage in doing so, but I opt for continuing to build an existing longer run over starting or adding to a smaller one (all other things being equal).
summary: K♦ on the waste ends the keep_options wait from #5 (a king can fill the column emptied); between the red 9s, 9♥ carries the longer run (9♥ 8♣ 7♦ 6♠), so 9♥f.

quote: Because my goal is to not use memory/card-counting, playing a king is an automatic play, similar to the reason for always playing an ace on its home pile.
summary: K♦a fills the column emptied at #12; automatic, like ace_home, under the no-memory rule.
Only other play was 8♣c (moving the run between 9s, nothing new), so draw.
